sections.title: Prospectus Summary
text: The following summary is qualified in its entirety by, and should be read in conjunction with, the more detailed information and financial statements included elsewhere in this prospectus. In addition to this summary, we urge you to read the entire prospectus carefully, especially the risks of investing in our Shares, discussed under “Risk Factors,” before deciding whether to buy our Ordinary Shares.

We are a professional, guitar-focused enterprise headquartered in Hong Kong, offering guitar-related technical, educational, and commercial services, as well as music event planning, management and performance services. Our business philosophy emphasizes sustainability and the long-term musical value of instruments. We seek to support musicians throughout the lifecycle of guitar ownership, from education and guitar-assembly workshops to acquisition and long-term care, while also providing music event services to a broader range of customers.

Our business is built on an integrated model that combines five principal activities: (i) guitar assembling workshops; (ii) repair and custom guitar services; (iii) guitar lessons; (iv) guitar trading; and (v) music events. We introduced custom guitar production and music events as new revenue streams in 2026. Our physical location at Unit 8-9 on the 19th Floor of the Westin Center at No. 26 Hung To Road, Kwun Tong, Kowloon, Hong Kong serves as the operational and experiential center of this integrated platform. The facility brings together our retail area, guitar repair and custom guitar activities, guitar assembling workshops, and instructional guitar lessons within a single venue in separate rooms, allowing customers to engage with our brand in a comprehensive and hands-on environment. Our music events are generally conducted at third-party venues selected based on the requirements of each event.

text: An investment in our Shares involves a high degree of risk. Before deciding whether to invest in our Ordinary Shares, you should consider carefully the risks described below, together with all of the other information set forth in this prospectus, including the sections titled “Business” and “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” and our consolidated financial statements and related notes. The risks described below and discussed in other parts of this prospectus, any prospectus supplement, any post-effective amendment or in any document incorporated by reference herein or therein are not the only ones that we face. Additional risks not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also affect our business. The following discussions should be read in conjunction with our financial statements and the notes to the financial statements included therein. You should only consider investing in our Ordinary Shares if you can bear the risk of loss of your entire investment.

Our business is sensitive to overall economic conditions, particularly because a significant portion of our revenue is derived from discretionary spending on our guitar assembly workshops, repair and instructional services, and instrument sales. A sustained decline in economic activity, reduced consumer confidence, or contraction in disposable income could lead to decreased demand for our products and services, delayed purchasing decisions by customers, and increased pricing pressure.

sections.title: Enforceability of Civil Liabilities
text: We are incorporated under the laws of the Cayman Islands because of certain benefits associated with being a Cayman Islands exempted company, such as political and economic stability, an effective judicial system, a favorable tax system, the absence of foreign exchange control or currency restrictions and the availability of professional and support services. However, the Cayman Islands has a less developed body of securities laws than the United States and provides less protection for investors. In addition, Cayman Islands companies may not have standing to sue before the federal courts of the United States.

All of our assets are located outside the United States. None of our directors and officers are U.S. citizens or residents. In addition, four of our five directors and officers are nationals or residents of Hong Kong. All or a substantial portion of our five directors’ and officers’ assets are located outside the United States. As a result, it may be difficult for investors to effect service of process within the United States upon us or these persons, or to enforce judgments obtained in U.S. courts against us or them, including judgments predicated upon the civil liability provisions of the securities laws of the United States or any state in the United States.

sections.title: Regulation
text: This section sets forth a summary of the most significant regulations or requirements that affect our business activities in Hong Kong or our shareholders’ right to receive dividends and other distributions from us.

The Business Registration Ordinance (Chapter 310 of the Laws of Hong Kong) requires every person carrying on any business in Hong Kong to apply for and obtain a business registration certificate from the Commissioner of Inland Revenue, unless it is exempt under the Business Registration Ordinance. Any person who fails to apply for business registration shall be guilty of an offence and shall be liable to a fine of HK$5,000 (approximately US$645) and to imprisonment for one year.

The Employment Ordinance (Chapter 57 of the Laws of Hong Kong) is the main piece of legislation enacted for, among other things, governing the general conditions of employment in Hong Kong. It provides for various employment-related benefits and protections, including but not limited to notice of termination of his or her employment contract, payment in lieu of notice, statutory holidays or alternative holidays, rest days, paid annual leave, sickness allowance, maternity protection, severance payments, and long service payments.

Under section 25 of the Employment Ordinance, where a contract of employment is terminated, any sum due to the employee shall be paid to him/her as soon as it is practicable and in any case not later than seven days after the day of termination. Any employer who willfully and without reasonable excuse contravenes section 25 of the Employment Ordinance commits an offence and is liable to a maximum fine of HK$350,000 (approximately US$45,200) and imprisonment for three years.

tax.text:
The Company is incorporated in the Cayman Islands. ocf.heading: Operating activities
ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities was $274,656 for the six months ended April 30, 2026, representing a significant increase compared to $49,345 for the six months ended April 30, 2025. This improvement was primarily driven by a substantial increase in net income, which grew to $41,637 for the six months ended April 30, 2026 from $6,571 for the six months ended April 30, 2025. Operating cash flow was stronger relative to bottom-line earnings, generating $274,656 in net operating cash against a net income of $41,637. The excess of operating cash flow over net income was principally attributable to changes in working capital, namely an increase of $170,417 in accrued expenses and other payables, which primarily reflected professional fees payable in connection with this Offering (other payables amounted to $152,425 as of April 30, 2026, compared with nil as of October 31, 2025), and an increase of $84,147 in tax payable, as no Hong Kong profits tax was paid during the period, partially offset by an increase of $26,923 in deposits and prepayments, mainly prepaid professional fees. Non-cash adjustments had a minimal net impact on operating cash flows.

costs.heading: Operating expenses
costs.text:
Total operating expenses increased by $635,062, or 341%, from $186,391 for the six months ended April 30, 2025, to $821,453 for the six months ended April 30, 2026. This growth was primarily driven by a sharp rise in legal and professional fees associated with our ongoing initial public offering (the “IPO”) preparation activities, which included accounting, audit, industry research, and professional advisory services for the proposed listing. The increase was further supported by branding and design fee related to the development of the brand strategy and design.

Selling and marketing expenses decreased by $21,775, or 15%, from $148,478 for the six months ended April 30, 2025, to $126,703 for the six months ended April 30, 2026. This decrease was primarily driven by decrease of marketing and promotional activities, specifically digital advertising and social media engagement.

General and administrative expenses increased by $656,837, or 1,732%, from $37,913 for the six months ended April 30, 2025 to $694,750 for the six months ended April 30, 2026. The increase was consistent with the Group’s ongoing IPO preparation activities, including accounting, audit, industry research and other professional advisory services incurred in connection with the proposed listing.

cor.heading: Cost of revenue
cor.text:
Cost of other revenue-generating activities

Cost of other revenue-generating activities, comprising costs associated with guitar assembling workshops, guitar repair and custom services, guitar lessons, guitar trading sales, amounted to $162,692 for the six months ended April 30, 2026, compared with $119,183 for the six months ended April 30, 2025, representing an increase of $43,509, or 37%. The increase was primarily attributable to higher levels of guitar assembling workshop and repair and custom activities.

The direct costs associated with our guitar-related service activities principally consist of directly attributable staff costs and, where applicable, materials and consumables. For our guitar assembling workshops, participants generally provide the principal materials used in assembling their guitars, which limits the amount of materials required to be provided by us. Guitar trading sales, in contrast, require us to incur costs associated with guitars, components, materials and/or inventory sold to customers and therefore have a different direct cost profile from our traditional service activities.

Cost of music events amounted to $530,862 for the six months ended April 30, 2026, compared with nil for the six months ended April 30, 2025, as we commenced our music event activities during the period.

gp.heading: Gross profit and gross profit margin
gp.text:
Gross profit increased by $ 751,416, or 383%, from $196,291 for the six months ended April 30, 2025 to $ 947,707 for the six months ended April 30, 2026, primarily as a result of the substantial increase in our total revenue during the period. Despite the increase in gross profit, our gross profit margin decreased by 4.5 percentage points, from 62.2% for the six months ended April 30, 2025 to 57.7% for the six months ended April 30, 2026.

The decrease in gross profit margin was primarily attributable to the significant change in our revenue mix following the introduction of music events during the period. Music events became our largest revenue stream, representing approximately 56.5% of our total revenue for the six months ended April 30, 2026. Unlike our traditional guitar-related service activities, private music events require us to incur event-specific costs, including performer fees, venue costs, equipment costs, event personnel, stage setup costs and other directly attributable costs, as applicable, resulting in a higher direct cost component relative to revenue.

nonop.heading: Other income and expenses
nonop.text: Other income and expenses decreased by $6,124, or 111%, from net other income of $5,516 for the six months ended April 30, 2025 to net other expenses of $608 for the six months ended April 30, 2026. This decrease was primarily attributable to the non-recurrence of a $6,154 gain on the extinguishment of asset retirement obligations recognized in the six months ended April 30, 2025, which accounted for substantially all of the net other income in that period. To a lesser extent, finance costs increased by $488, from $677 to $1,165, reflecting a full six months of interest on the bank borrowings under the SME Financing Guarantee Scheme, which were drawn down during the six months ended April 30, 2025.
